bug_semantics: A Shell-mode action may declare an argument type beginning with regex:. The custom pattern is checked with regexp.MatchString, but checkShellArgumentSafety historically compared only exact names in a fixed unsafe-type map and therefore allowed every regex:-prefixed type. The accepted attacker value is inserted without shell quoting into the configured command and executed through sh -c. Thus a value such as $(touch /tmp/rce_proof) passes a superficially restrictive regex that excludes ;|&<> when the pattern permits $, parentheses, and the command text, then executes by POSIX command substitution. Partial-match regex behavior could widen the bypass further, but is not required for the advisory's command-substitution attack.
flaw_origin: The smallest reconstructable source commit is PR #244 member 90cf98357843a303153525cd117d9ca5b5bf48fc. Against parent 2fb40ff44312b310aa11f85db0de1a641ee245ec it newly makes typeSafetyCheckRegex accept arbitrary regex:-prefixed argument types and use the suffix as the validation pattern. The parent already substituted validated values directly into shell command text and executed it via sh -c, but rejected unknown regex: types, so the new custom-regex acceptance completed the vulnerable path. GitHub landed the exact same tree and parent as single-parent squash c97fd60c2508ddf99ebc7c03570683811c476de9; later move ff31abe66cfd46f8cccca00ad708529e4d920144 only relocated internal/executor/arguments.go to service/internal/executor/arguments.go. Main-line commit c917d1b1e7a2a90acec79760cb1ff18ffae82409 later introduced Exec and checkShellArgumentSafety but omitted regex: from its exact-name blocklist, preserving rather than originating the custom-regex injection.

reasoning: The exploitable capability begins when the one-member PR commit enables arbitrary regex: argument types in a system that already performs unquoted shell-string substitution. Its direct parent cannot accept such a type, so parent absence is directly established. The later incomplete shell-safety allow/deny split explains the advisory's stated bypass and remains vulnerable through 3000.16.2, while direct fix 0e45f3b0e3c9e81685bc85b7c4f21187bb0df085 and merge 995ff79736f2bccc364448a3ece84087b550b232 close the prefix bypass for 3000.17.0. The true decomposed BIC commit object has only human identities and no AI disclosure or bot marker. The only explicit AI signal in this lifecycle is on the fix, which the protocol requires ignoring. Therefore the causal result is NOT_AI.
